mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly increases discount rates for equity valuation, reducing equity prices and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0% (2-year rolling window Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals a tightening labor market that accelerates inflation and triggers Federal Reserve rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 4.0% (2-year rolling window Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise (2-year rolling window Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained economy (INDPRO < 100), a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates improving supply conditions, reducing inflation fears and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO rises in a supply-constrained economy (INDPRO < 100) (2-year rolling window Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of employment growth (PAYEMS) directly supports consumer spending and corporate revenue, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average (2-year rolling window Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates a supply shock that increases inflation and prompts aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100 (2-year rolling window Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 320), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates aggressive monetary tightening to combat inflation, compressing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 320 and FEDFUNDS rises (2-year rolling window Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 > 22750), a slowdown in quarterly GDP growth (indicated by declining GDPC1 from prior quarter) signals an economic peak and potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 > 22750 and GDPC1 declines from prior quarter (2-year rolling window Rank IC < 0.03).
